subject: Recap + next steps: long-context eval, truncation behavior, and model options

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Recap + next steps: long-context eval, truncation behavior, and model options

Hi Thomas — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: Determine whether Redwood can reliably summarize and extract structured insights from patient records and multi-doc clinical narratives that are ~40k-60k tokens long, with minimal hallucination and conservative truncation behavior.
- Success criteria you shared: (1) <5% factual hallucination on summary gold standard, (2) end-to-end latency under 2.5s per 1k tokens for extract pipeline (batched), (3) ability to pin model version and roll back on regression.

Action items we committed to: 
1) SE team will run a targeted long-context eval using a 1k-real-doc sample you provided (anonymized), focusing on summarization fidelity and prefix-preservation behavior. Deliverables: benchmark CSV + example prompt sets.
2) We'll recommend two model variants to try: a 64k-window variant (quantized if needed) and a fall-back 8k variant with a chunking+cross-attention stitching approach.
3) Pricing/ops: propose a pilot committed capacity month with a reduced compute rate for evaluation runs; we'll send a quote once scope is final.

I've asked Grace to lead the technical run and attach the initial results and prompt sets by EOD Friday. If that timeline doesn't work for you, please say so. Also, please confirm whether we should evaluate on the full anonymized corpus or a stratified subset (legal docs, clinical notes, imaging reports).

Thanks — Karthik

--

Subject: RE: Recap + next steps: long-context eval, truncation behavior, and model options

Hi Thomas — following up with the SE plan and the first-pass artifacts. Summary of what we ran and early observations: 

What we evaluated (attached "longctx-benchmarks.csv"):
- Dataset: 150 anonymized clinical narratives (mix: discharge summaries, consult notes, multi-section reports). Avg length = 48k tokens, median = 41k.
- Tasks: (A) concise summary (200-400 tokens), (B) structured extraction (10 key-value fields), (C) change-detection across appended encounter notes.
- Metrics: ROUGE-L for summary overlap, token-level hallucination rate (benchmarked against manual labels), F1 for extraction.

Models/configs tested (high level):
- rdx-m-64k-v1 (float16): native 64k context window; baseline for fidelity.
- rdx-m-64k-q4 (quantized): Q4 quantized variant to measure perf/cost tradeoffs.
- rdx-s-8k-stitch (8k): 8k native window with chunk+stitch summarization (context stitching by vector-based retrieval + cross-chunk attention stitching).

Key findings (first pass):
- Fidelity: rdx-m-64k-v1 produced the highest ROUGE-L on summaries (avg 0.72) and lowest measured hallucination (~4.6%).
- Quantized: rdx-m-64k-q4 had a small fidelity delta (ROUGE-L -0.03 on average) but reduced token cost by ~35%. Hallucination rose to ~6.2% in edge cases where numeric details were present.
- Stitching approach: rdx-s-8k-stitch performed well on extraction tasks (F1 ~0.81) but summaries showed coherence drift on very long timelines — useful as fallback for cost-sensitive workloads.
- Truncation behavior: default runtime preserves most recent tokens and will evict older KV-cache segments when capacity is exceeded. For summarization fidelity we recommend prefix-preservation via our pinned-prefix option or progressive KV snapshotting (we included a sample config).

Attached artifacts:
- longctx-benchmarks.csv (benchmark metrics + per-document rows)
- eval-prompt-sets.jsonl (prompt templates, system prompts, and example few-shot contexts we used)
- ava-longctx-eval-summary.pdf (2-page executive summary)

Recommended next steps:
1) Try rdx-m-64k-q4 on a 1-week pilot (we can provision dedicated capacity). We will keep rdx-m-64k-v1 available as a rollback if you see fidelity regressions.
2) Provide a labeled 200-doc goldset for a stricter hallucination measurement (we can run the evaluation and produce per-field regression alerts).
3) If cost is the primary constraint, iterate on stitching + reranking and set up targeted quality alerts on numeric fields.

Links: evaluation notebook (https://notebooks.redwood.ai/longctx-eval/ava-2026), prompt set in Drive (attached), HubSpot record for the deal: hubspot:contact:HS-984321.

Happy to jump on a 30-min technical call with your ML lead to walk through the prompt sets and stitching approach. Available Mon/Tue next week.

Best,
Grace

From: Thomas Hart <thomas.hart@avasolutions.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 08:29:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: long-context eval, truncation behavior, and model options

Thanks, Grace — this is helpful. A few clarifying q's before we schedule the ML deep-dive: 

1) Our corpus includes many documents with embedded tables and timeline sections where numeric fidelity is critical. For the quantized variant, can you share an example where the -0.03 ROUGE-L and the +1.6% hallucination were observed (i.e., specific failure modes)?

2) On the stitching approach: does the stitching pipeline preserve cross-chunk co-reference (patients, dates) reliably? Example: when a condition is mentioned in the first chunk and later updated in the 10th, will the stitched summary reflect the latest state or collapse to the earliest mention?

3) Truncation: you mentioned pinned-prefix and KV snapshotting. If we enable pinned-prefix for the opening 5k tokens (legal header + critical patient identifiers), what is the incremental cost and impact on throughput?

4) Finally, for the pilot quote — can you give a rough per-token estimate for rdx-m-64k-q4 vs rdx-s-8k-stitch so we can budget before the committed capacity proposal?

If it's easier, we can do the 30-min technical call — would prefer Wed 10am PT.

Regards,
Thomas
Ava Solutions
thomas.hart@avasolutions.com

Dev / Grace — forwarding Thomas's questions from Ava Solutions (below). Please propose concise answers we can send before Wed 10am PT and prep a 30-min slot for the ML lead call. I think we should: 

- Include an annotated example (from the benchmark CSV) that highlights a quantization failure mode (numeric drift) and a mitigation (post-hoc reranking on numeric fields or use v1 float variant).
- For stitching co-reference: provide a short technical note that explains our cross-chunk attention stitching, recent tests on co-reference stable over 90% of cases for timelines, and when to prefer the 64k model.
- For pinned-prefix cost: a short table showing throughput deltas (tokens/sec) and estimated cost uplift for reserving 5k pinned tokens on a single request. Grace — can you paste the perf numbers and the pilot per-token ballparks for both variants?

I want a reply we can send to Thomas by Monday EOD (but Wed 10am PT is likely fine). Also please add the annotated CSV row as an attachment and mark it in the HubSpot timeline.

Thanks — Karthik

--
